FACT_ID: sec13-R01 | anchor: A01
Failing to yield to a pedestrian in a crosswalk is four points, while failing to yield to an ambulance, fire truck or police officer is five points [A01].
Why it matters: group point values; difficulty high; prereq sec13-F05; confusables sec13-F05, sec13-F06
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec13-R02 | anchor: A01
Speeding and texting both carry point ranges, two to eight for speeding by how far over the limit and two to five for texting, unlike the fixed values of the other listed offenses [A01].
Why it matters: group point values; difficulty medium; prereq sec13-F02; confusables sec13-F02, sec13-F03
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec13-R03 | anchor: A01
Ten points is the suspension trigger, while the two year window is what decides how long the suspension lasts [A01].
Why it matters: group suspension; difficulty medium; prereq sec13-F08; confusables sec13-F08, sec13-F09
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec13-R04 | anchor: A01
Running a red light costs two points, but failing to obey a police officer costs four [A01].
Why it matters: group point values; difficulty low; prereq sec13-F04; confusables sec13-F04, sec13-F05
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0065]
